messages:
Maria Gomez: Heads up — p99 tail latency spike on llama-3-13b pool after the kernel-prefork tweak this morning. Seeing ~+180ms on long contexts (>1k tokens). profiling artifact linked below.
perf-bot: Perf job 22345 finished. Summary: p50 +2ms, p95 +45ms, p99 +180ms vs baseline. Artifact: s3://redwood-perf/22345/profile.tar.gz :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Alex Chen: @Maria can you paste the small flame snippet or top hotspots? suspect KV prefetch or a kernel selection path flip. :thinking:
Maria Gomez: quick flame snippet from the profile (top samples):
```
kv_prefetch_worker: 62%
matmul_fuse_kernel: 18%
memcpy (GPU<->CPU): 8%
other: 12%
```
Vikram Rao: we turned on kernel-prefork to warm kernels earlier. That + aggressive KV prefetch could change the sequence sizes we hit and force different kernels (nvfused vs matmul_fuse). Also head-dim alignment sometimes nudges kernel_selector thresholds. @Alex did your PR touch kernel routing thresholds?
Alex Chen: yeah PR #4876 adjusted thresholds for head_dim=64 to prefer nvfused fallback when batch_shape aligned. Merged ~6am yesterday. Rolling it back would be a quick A/B.
Sam Jenkins: I'll spin a canary with env overrides: `KERNEL_PREFORK=0 KV_PREFETCH_BATCH=16` and run chat-template long-context workload.
Maria Gomez: started canary canary-pp-3 on dev cluster, routing 1k chat template requests (~1000 contexts). Initial run pushed 1k requests.
perf-bot: Canary run 22345-canary results: p99 down ~140ms, p95 down ~40ms. Kernel selection stats: `matmul_fuse_kernel` selected for 78% of canary requests vs 22% in prod; nvfused selected less.
Alex Chen: that matches the theory — kernel-selector change moved many requests to nvfused path which under these contexts is worse. Reverting PR for head_dim=64 makes sense.
Vikram Rao: I'll also add a small CI microbenchmark: vary head_dim in {32,64,80,96} and run KV cache alignment + 1200-token chat template to catch regressions. Also add a probe that logs kernel ids for long decodes.
Maria Gomez: Filed INF-1123 with links to profile, canary logs, and the rollback PR suggestion. Thanks everyone. :eyes:
Alex Chen: I'll open the rollback PR now and include a short note about kernel-prefork interactions.
Sam Jenkins: After rollback we should run a couple of mixed workload runs (short/long contexts) before re-enabling prefork.
Maria Gomez: Agreed. Leaving this thread open until rollback + CI tests pass. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
